rules.statement: A surviving spouse, who has made a will jointly with a predeceased spouse as regards their common property, and has been appointed heir to such predeceased spouse, cannot make a different disposition in respect of that portion of the common property which ought to revert to the substitutes of the predeceased; but as regards that portion which would devolve on his own heirs he may legally make a disposition, unless both the spouses have by common consent made a disposition of the common estate or of the share of the survivor.
rules.supporting_quote: "A surviving spouse, who has made a will jointly with a predeceased spouse as regards their common property, and has been appointed heir to such predeceased spouse, cannot make a different disposition in respect of that portion of the common property which ought to revert to the substitutes of the predeceased; but as regards that portion which would devolve on his own heirs he may legally make a disposition, unless both the spouses have by common consent made a disposition of the common estate or of the share of the survivor." (Van der Keessel in Juta L. C. 2, pp. Ill, 167-168)
